# Estate review: Batch 1 of 3

Nothing is saved or changed yet. On the unchanged inputs, `phase0 check` passes and all 3 tests pass. I haven't dry-run these edits; how they apply comes from reading the executor code.

| Kind | Live now | Input size | Already omitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rules | 80 (57 obligation, 23 prod-only) | 5.6 KB of rule text, 22 KB pin | T-81 to T-85 |
| Obligations | 59 entries (56 active, 1 waived, 1 deferred, 1 split parent) | 60.6 KB | I-54 |
| Ledger | 39 entries | 2.7 KB | C-39 |
| Open debt | 15 | 6.7 KB rendered | none |

**Biggest problem, which compaction can't fix:** the obligations claim far more than the product does.
- **Missing tests:** 55 of the 56 active obligations name a witness test that doesn't exist; only `I-20` does. `phase0 check` doesn't catch this because it checks witness files, not test ids.
- **Missing features:** `src/` has no code for slips, audit trails, sessions, locks, tokens, archive or date validation.
- **Slips:** I-21 is marked must-hold with a "proves" judgment, but it's unbuilt. It should be `future`, delivered by the `slips` unit.
- **Contradicted rules:** T-5 and T-6 require exit 2 on a missing id, but `list` and `export` exit 0, and the `list` test expects that output.

So the no-loss checks below compare rule text only, because almost no test backs either side. This needs its own decision at Phase 0.

**Left alone on purpose:** T-20, I-20 and C-34 (recent findings F-1 and F-2), T-21 and I-21 (the current slice), and T-72 (your P-1 answer).

## Decisions

1. retire T-8
   - Items: T-8 and I-8, "The PortLink SOAP bridge retries failed deliveries every ten minutes."
   - Replacement: none
   - Gives up: the ten-minute delivery retry
   - Why: the bridge was removed, and `src/` and `test/` no longer mention PortLink. B-2 follows in Batch 2.

2. retire T-33
   - Items: T-33 and I-33, "Dispatch is allowed until 72 hours before the tide (working assumption P-1)."
   - Replacement: none, T-72 stays as written ("Dispatch is allowed until 48 hours before the tide."). P-1's `bears` moves from T-33 to T-72, and its recorded answer is unchanged.
   - Gives up: the 72-hour cutoff, and the only obligation on any dispatch cutoff
   - Why: your P-1 answer replaced it.
   - T-72 is prod-only and the product has no dispatch code, so nothing will test the cutoff. I'd accept that until dispatch exists.

3. retire T-27
   - Items: T-27 and I-27, "The export command refuses invalid dates."
   - Replacement: none, T-41 stays as written ("Every command refuses invalid dates before reading or writing records.")
   - Gives up: nothing; T-41 covers export and is stricter
   - Why: it duplicates T-41.
   - I-41's future test must include export, or this property goes unproven.

4. merge T-3 and T-14
   - Items: T-3 and I-3, "A berth booking identifier is unique across the register."; T-14 and I-14, "No two entries in the register have the same berth booking identifier."
   - Replacement: T-3 and I-3, text unchanged; T-14 and I-14 retire
   - Gives up: nothing; both demand one identifier per entry across the whole register
   - Why: same claim, worded twice.
   - The `I-20` test already checks for duplicates. I-3 keeps its own missing witness id, because dropping that id would be refused as a weakening.

5. retire T-52
   - Items: T-52, "Comment text is grammatical English."; I-52, "One internal comment is grammatical English."
   - Replacement: none
   - Gives up: any demand on comment grammar
   - Why: `src/` has no comments, the requirement is trivial, and the two texts don't even agree.

6. retire T-62
   - Items: T-62 (prod-only), "Internal local variable names use lower camel case."
   - Replacement: none
   - Gives up: the naming requirement; the current code complies, but nothing would hold future code to it
   - Why: it's a style preference with no bearing on either vision clause.

7. retire T-63
   - Items: T-63 (prod-only), "The command must be implemented in executable program instructions."
   - Replacement: none
   - Gives up: nothing
   - Why: any working command already meets it.

8. retire T-70
   - Items: T-70 (prod-only), "The welcome banner ends with a period."
   - Replacement: none
   - Gives up: the punctuation of a banner, if one is ever added
   - Why: the product has no banner.

9. tighten T-49
   - Items: T-49, "In order to ensure that the operator can rely on the output when things go wrong, every failed command, without exception, prints its diagnostic to stderr rather than to stdout."
   - Replacement: T-49, same id: "Every failed command prints its diagnostic to stderr, not stdout." The reason moves to prose in `register.md`: "Operators rely on command output when things go wrong, so diagnostics stay off stdout."
   - Gives up: nothing; "every" covers "without exception", and the stderr and not-stdout demands both stay
   - Why: same meaning in fewer words.
   - I-49 keeps its long statement for now, because Phase 0 refuses a statement edit on an active obligation (`plugin/executor/src/preflight/checks.ts:563`). Shortening it later takes a post-start CAS apply, rev 2 and a fresh proof judgment, which needs a real test first.

## Result if all nine pass

- **Rules:** 80 to 72.
- **Active obligations:** 56 to 51. I-8, I-14, I-27, I-33 and I-52 must carry a `retired` state with a reason naming their K-n through `arc-next`, because Phase 0 refuses removing an active one outright. They drop out the arc after, taking entries from 59 to 54.
- **Prose:** I'd also remove the `register.md` sentences about T-33 and T-27, since they'd be out of date.

## Still to come

- **Batch 2, ledger and debt:** C-23, C-30, C-38 and the token and archive folds, plus B-2, B-6, B-11 and the index debt. C-12 and C-38 are cited by `slips.json`, so those citations change too.
- **Batch 3, command-by-command rule families:** most of these have gaps, such as no missing-id rule for `arrive` or `search`. An "every command" merge would quietly add requirements, so these need enumerated replacements. The sorting family can't merge cleanly at all, because I-54, I-55 and I-56 are retired, waived and deferred.

I recommend approving all nine. Reply "approve all", or give the numbers to approve, change or reject, and I'll record the approved ones in `../roadmap-inputs/drafts/compaction.md` before starting Batch 2.
reply:
1: approve
2: approve
3: approve
4: approve; T-3 and I-3 wording stays: "A berth booking identifier is unique across the register."
5: reject as written. Approve retiring I-52 only; keep T-52. Accepted loss: the separate test demanding grammatical English in one internal comment.
6: approve
7: approve
8: reject; keep T-70.
9: reject the proposed wording. Approve tightening T-49 with this exact wording: "Every failed command prints its diagnostic to stderr, never stdout."

# Estate review: Batch 2

Your Batch 1 decisions are recorded as K-1 to K-8 in `../roadmap-inputs/drafts/compaction.md`, with your exact wording for T-3 and T-49. T-70 stays and isn't recorded; T-52 stays and only I-52 retires.

Rules are now headed from 80 to 74, and active obligations from 56 to 51.

I made two small calls while recording, and either is easy to change:
- **T-52 census state (K-5):** keeping the rule without an obligation needs a new state, so I used `untestable`.
- **T-49 reason (K-8):** I kept the reason sentence from my proposal as prose in `register.md`, since you only rewrote the rule. It reads "Operators rely on command output when things go wrong, so diagnostics stay off stdout."

This batch covers all 15 debt items and six ledger entries. Its K and C ids assume all ten pass; if any don't, I'll renumber and show you the new text before recording.

## Decisions

1. resolve B-2
   - Items: B-2, "Remove the retry queue in the PortLink SOAP bridge."
   - Replacement: `C-41 — B-2 resolved by compaction K-9: the PortLink bridge is gone; retry-queue cleanup is given up.`
   - Gives up: retry-queue cleanup in the removed bridge
   - Why: the bridge no longer exists, and the draft `keep` reason in `phase0.json` talks about index work, which doesn't apply to it.

2. resolve B-6
   - Items: B-6, "Index reserve record lookup; B-1 already tracks the same index."
   - Replacement: `C-42 — B-6 resolved by compaction K-10: it duplicates B-1 and demands nothing further.`
   - Gives up: nothing
   - Why: it says itself that it duplicates B-1.

3. resolve B-11
   - Items: B-11, "Align the success message punctuation with the help footer."
   - Replacement: `C-43 — B-11 resolved by compaction K-11: the product has no help footer and success output is the bare record id; punctuation alignment is given up.`
   - Gives up: aligning success punctuation with a help footer, if one is ever added
   - Why: there's nothing to align today.
   - You kept T-70, so if you want output punctuation tracked, reject this one.

4. resolve B-1, B-3, B-4, B-5, B-7 and B-8
   - Items: "Add an index for `<command>` record lookup to avoid scanning the register on every call.", for reserve, arrive, depart, list, inspect and search in that order
   - Replacement: `C-44 — B-1, B-3, B-4, B-5, B-7 and B-8 resolved by compaction K-12: each command reads the whole JSON register, so a lookup index saves little; linear record lookup is left unfixed.`
   - Gives up: indexed record lookup; every command keeps scanning
   - Why: `src/cli.js` loads the entire file on each call anyway. I haven't measured this, and no rule or vision clause sets a speed requirement.

5. resolve B-9, B-10, B-12, B-13, B-14 and B-15
   - Items: "Add an index for `<command>` audit lookup to avoid scanning the register on every call.", for reserve, cancel, depart, list, export and inspect in that order
   - Replacement: `C-45 — B-9, B-10, B-12, B-13, B-14 and B-15 resolved by compaction K-13: the product has no audit trail to index; audit lookup indexes are given up.`
   - Gives up: planned audit lookup indexes; they'd need raising again once an audit trail exists
   - Why: there's nothing to index. The audit rules T-42 to T-48 are unaffected.

6. retire C-23
   - Items: C-23, "The first release demo uses the blue harbour slide template."
   - Replacement: none
   - Gives up: the template choice for that demo
   - Why: the cut line says the previous release is complete, and nothing else cites this entry.
   - I'm assuming that release was the first one. If that demo is still ahead, reject this.

7. retire C-30
   - Items: C-30, "Retire the old walkthrough obligation I-54."
   - Replacement: none
   - Gives up: the live ledger note for why I-54 left; `arc-previous` and git history still have it
   - Why: I-54 is already gone from `arc-next`, and nothing there cites C-30. C-31 and C-32 stay because I-55 and I-56 still cite them.

8. retire C-38
   - Items: C-38, "Temporary trace output is permitted for this arc only."
   - Replacement: none; remove `C-38` from `cites.rulings` in `slips.json`. C-40 stays as written ("Trace output redacts operator credentials.").
   - Gives up: permission for temporary trace output
   - Why: the arc that permission covered is finished, the product has no trace output, and the slips acceptance doesn't touch tracing.

9. fold C-12 and C-17
   - Items: C-12, "A request token is accepted once; retries return the stored response."; C-17, "Retries with the same request token return the stored response without another mutation."
   - Replacement: `T-86: A request token is accepted once; retries with the same token return the stored response without another mutation.` The census state is `out-of-slice`. Remove both ledger lines and remove `C-12` from `cites.rulings` in `slips.json`.
   - Gives up: nothing; checked accepted once, same-token retries, stored response, and no further mutation
   - Why: your notes call the token policy a standing truth, so it belongs in the corpus as one rule.
   - The product has no token code. As a corpus rule, whole-target audits will read it, but `out-of-slice` means no test is required yet.

10. fold C-4
    - Items: C-4, "The Quaybook archive is append-only; corrections add a new revision."
    - Replacement: `T-87: The Quaybook archive is append-only; corrections add a new revision.` The census state is `out-of-slice`. Remove the ledger line.
    - Gives up: nothing; same text
    - Why: your notes call the archive policy a standing truth too.
    - The product has no archive code, so the same audit note as T-86 applies.

## Result if all ten pass

| Kind | Now | After Batches 1 and 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Rules | 80 | 76 (74 + T-86, T-87) |
| Active obligations | 56 | 51 |
| Ledger entries | 39 | 38 (6 removed, 5 added) |
| Open debt | 15 | 0 |

The ledger barely shrinks here because each resolve adds a line. The real reduction comes next.

## Still to come

- **Batch 3:** merging the ledger's per-command families, C-1 to C-37. These keep their exact command lists: for example, the session and lock families have never covered `depart`, and I won't add it without asking.
- **Batch 3 or 4:** the rule families, which is where most of the remaining obligation size sits.

I recommend approving all ten, with 3 and 6 as the two that need your judgment.
